sentences.text: Linhenykus was a small, extinct alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Inner Mongolia, China, reaching a length of approximately 70 cm.

Its femur measures 7 cm in length, and it is the first known alvarezsaurid to possess only a single, second digit on its forelimbs, a unique reduction compared to other species that typically retain reduced first and third digits.
Linhenykus holds the distinction of being the first alvarezsaurid discovered with a completely monodactyl hand, featuring just one finger.
Despite its tiny stature of about 70 cm, the animal possessed a femur measuring 7 cm, highlighting its miniature proportions.
The fossil was collected by Jonah N. Choiniere and Michael Pittman and was first described and named in 2011 by Xu Xing, Corwin Sullivan, and seven other researchers.
Linhenykus belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae and is the parent group of the subfamily Parvicursorinae, where it is classified as the most basal known member.
Linhenykus monodactylus is the only known species of this extinct genus.

The fossil was found in the Upper Campanian Wulansuhai Formation, dating to between 84 and 75 million years ago, placing the animal in the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
It has been debated whether Linhenykus is a junior synonym of Parvicursor, but this view was rejected by the original authors and subsequent researchers.
